parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Sodium nitrite, $\text{NaNO}_2$, is a decomposition product from heating sodium nitrate, $\text{NaNO}_3$.

A student analysed a sample of sodium nitrite by titration with aqueous cerium(IV) ions, $\text{Ce}^{4+}\text{(aq)}$. The equation for the titration reaction is shown.

$$\text{NO}_2^-\text{(aq)} + 2\text{Ce}^{4+}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow 2\text{Ce}^{3+}\text{(aq)} + \text{NO}_3^-\text{(aq)} + 2\text{H}^+\text{(aq)}$$

- $0.138\text{ g}$ of impure sodium nitrite was dissolved in water and made up to $100\text{ cm}^3$ in a volumetric flask.
- $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of this solution required $21.80\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0400\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Ce}^{4+}\text{(aq)}$ to reach the end-point.

You should assume the impurity does not react with $\text{Ce}^{4+}\text{(aq)}$.

Calculate the percentage purity of the sample of sodium nitrite.
